matt: FYI seeing a spike of fncall rejects across a couple enterprise tenants. They all look like the tool returned a different shape (array vs object) and our strict per-route schema is dropping them.
anya: can you paste a minimal example of what was returned?
matt: sure — this is the captured payload that failed validation:
{"tool":"price_lookup","response":[{"sku":"A1","price":9.99},{"sku":"B2","price":null}]}
matt: our schema expects an object `{"items": {"sku":..., "price":...}}` so arrays get rejected
rachel: console only shows `validation_reject` counts, no route_id or customer token in the row to quickly map to owner. makes debugging slow :/ 
ben: adding route_id to the event would make it trivial but worried about leaking internal routing metadata to frontend analytics — can we keep it server-side?
kelsey: we can surface it in the console backend only (no export), or show owner-friendly label (team name) instead of raw route id. also maybe add a link to sampled payloads.
anya: we should also record `validation_reason` with the event (e.g., `array_instead_of_object`, `missing_required_field`) so that the dashboard can group failure modes.
matt: +1. current metric too coarse. we only get counts and a few random examples in the logs.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-19T18:22:13 by @kelsey toggled `fncall.strict_validation`=true on canary
rachel: that canary flip is the likely root cause of the spike — customers using older SDKs will break if we enable strict validation globally.
ben: product question — do we want strict validation to be billable failures? currently we charge tokens even when we return a validation rejection. implies customers get billed while their tool didn't actually run.
kelsey: proposal: soft-validate rollout plan:
 1) Add `fncall.validation.reason` telemetry and `route_meta` (server-only) to events.
 2) When strict_validation is enabled in canary, set `billing.on_validation_reject=false` for that slice.
 3) Enable sampling of full tool responses for 1 hour on failing routes (rate-limited) so we can triage shapes without full retention.
 4) Add console panel "Tool call rejects" that groups by `validation_reason` and shows top 10 routes.
anya: and a UX note — console should show a quick toggle per-route: `strict / lenient` with a tooltip explaining billing and compat implications.
matt: agree. also need an alert rule: `increase(fncall.validation.reject_count[5m]) > 50` that pages SRE for platform regressions (not tenant issues).
kelsey: noted. SRE can add a maintenance filter to ignore customer-bounded spikes.
ben: edge case: some customers intentionally return arrays and then our adapters convert into canonical shape. we should add an adapter layer for common mismatches before failing.achel: can we ship adapter heuristics behind `fncall.adapter_mode=permissive` so we test adapters without surprising clients?
kelsey: yes. plan: deliver telemetry and sampling this week, attach a canary where strict_validation=true and billing=false for that canary, observe rejects grouped by reason, then iterate adapters for top 3 failure reasons.
matt: thumbs up. I'll draft an RFC for the adapter heuristics and the console mockups.
anya: I can own the telemetry schema: event names `fncall.validation.reject`, `fncall.validation.sampled_response` with fields `route_key`, `validation_reason`, `sdk_version`.
ben: last ask: update billing docs and surface a console banner during rollout so customers don't get surprised by billing behavior changing.
rachel: thanks — if we get the `validation_reason` and sampled payload link in console it's going to save dozens of manual investigations :thumbsup:
kelsey: I'll create the canary and the config toggle. keeping this on the eng-platform board as P1 infra work.
